headline: NEW -- Iranian Army Ground Forces commander orders highest combat readiness
dek: Jahanshahi ordered all unit commanders to maintain the highest level of combat readiness via continuous training, readiness assessments, inter-unit coordination and correction of vulnerabilities, warning that in wartime 'any negligence or carelessness can carry heavy costs' and that the enemy…
sources: Brig Gen Ali Jahanshahi, commander of Iranian Army Ground Forces (Tasnim, IRNA, IRIB; relayed by Al Jazeera, Dawn liveblog)
fault_line: Deterrence signal vs invasion prep: is Tehran bracing for the post-midterm strike wave, or posturing for domestic/regional audiences?

sections.what_happened: Jahanshahi ordered all unit commanders to maintain the highest level of combat readiness via continuous training, readiness assessments, inter-unit coordination and correction of vulnerabilities, warning that in wartime 'any negligence or carelessness can carry heavy costs' and that the enemy seeks to disrupt armed-forces cohesion through hybrid threats. Issued as Trump publicly weighed 'finish it off' vs 'let it wither' on the Iran war the same day.
sections.what_verified: Tasnim via Eastora/Hatha Alyoum/tribune.pk; IRNA English; IRIB via Al Jazeera; Dawn liveblog 07:44pm
sections.what_disputed: No independent confirmation of actual force-posture change; readiness orders are routine Iranian signaling and may be declaratory rather than operational. (YouTube channel Azad Bol India embellished this with unverified details — bunker movement, live-round chambering — not supported by the state-media texts.)
sections.why_matters: Tehran's ground forces go to maximum alert the same day Trump asks out loud whether to 'finish it off' or 'let it wither.' The numbers: 51 combat units and 39,000 personnel were deployed to stop a ground invasion earlier (ABNA Oct 13). The question: is this the countdown to the post-midterm wave — or the signal that deters it?
sections.context: Background: NEW -- Iranian Army Ground Forces commander orders highest combat readiness; warns negligence in wartime 'carries heavy costs'

totw_analysis: Our read: Tehran's ground forces go to maximum alert the same day Trump asks out loud whether to 'finish it off' or 'let it wither.' The numbers: 51 combat units and 39,000 personnel were deployed to stop a ground invasion earlier (ABNA Oct 13). The question: is this the countdown to the post-midterm wave — or the signal that deters it?
